title: Sum of Unique Elements
spaceBreakdown:
- int cnt[101]: fixed 101 ints, independent of n → O(1)
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector, returned int
approach: Count how many times each value appears using a fixed-size frequency array indexed by value (valid because nums[i] ≤ 100). Then walk the value range 1..100 and add every value whose count is exactly 1. This is correct because the problem defines "unique" as appearing exactly once, and the count array directly records that property for every possible value.
hints: For each distinct value in nums, what single fact about its occurrences must you know before deciding whether it belongs in the final sum? The values are bounded by 100.
Use a frequency array of size 101 indexed by value. In [1,2,3,2], after counting, value 2 has frequency 2 so it is skipped; 1 and 3 each have frequency 1 and are added.

**Single element** - n = 1, the only element is unique.
`Input: nums = [5]` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: declaring `int cnt[100]` (indices 0..99) and indexing by value → out-of-bounds for value 100, returns undefined/garbage.

**All equal** - every value appears more than once.
`Input: nums = [1,1,1,1,1]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: summing values with `cnt[v] >= 1` instead of `== 1` → returns 1.

**Largest value** - nums[i] can equal 100.
`Input: nums = [100]` → `Expected: 100`
⚠️ Bug: looping `for v in 1..99` (off-by-one on the upper bound) → returns 0.

**All unique** - no duplicates at all.
`Input: nums = [1,2,3,4,5]` → `Expected: 15`
⚠️ Bug: adding v when `cnt[v] > 1` (inverted condition, summing only duplicates) → returns 0.

followUps.q: What if nums[i] can be up to 10^9 instead of 100?
followUps.a: Replace the fixed frequency array with an unordered_map<int,int>. Time stays O(n) expected; space becomes O(n) in the worst case when all values are distinct.

followUps.q: What if you must return the sum of elements appearing exactly k times, for a given k?
followUps.a: Keep the same counting pass; in the summation pass add v when cnt[v] == k. Time O(n), space O(1) since values are still ≤ 100.

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as a stream too large to store and you may only make one pass?
followUps.a: Exact one-pass uniqueness is impossible: a value seen once may reappear later, so you cannot finalize its contribution until the stream ends. You need either two passes (storing the stream) or external storage of counts.
